code: C# product code: HorizonMask.Compute (720 azimuths, 80 m steps, 250 km) + Analysis.Timeline (16-strip disk vs skyline, Sun size from distance, eclipses), hourly
reference: NASA PGDA product 69 (Mazarico), AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 (+_EARTH) when the site is inside it, else AVGVISIB_75S_120M_201608; values in tools/validation/pgda.json.

thresholds.note: Pass/fail rules for the C# validation (N1/N8). Written and committed BEFORE the first C# run, so they cannot be tuned to the results. Failures are reported, not hidden.
thresholds.reference: NASA PGDA product 69 (Mazarico), AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 (+_EARTH) when the site is inside it, else AVGVISIB_75S_120M_201608; values in tools/validation/pgda.json.
thresholds.comparison: C# product code (HorizonMask.Compute + Analysis.Timeline, hourly over the whole ephem.csv), observer at 0 m, Sun up = any part of the disk (sunFrac > 0), Earth in view = earthFrac > 0. PGDA is a surface map with the same 'any part of the disc' definition.

perSite.explainedRule: |diff| > 5 but our value is inside the PGDA 3x3 range +-5, or PGDA is inside our +-80 m (8 neighbours) range +-5

pass.why: the Python reimplementation gave 26/31 and 28/31; the C# must reproduce it within one site

csharpVsPython.rows: 0 m vs pgda.json ours0m, 2 m and 10 m vs ours.json (sunEdge, earthEdge)
csharpVsPython.caveat: known before running: since PR 26 the C# compares 16 strips of the disk with the real skyline, scales the Sun with distance and removes eclipses; the Python does not. A difference above 0.05 is reported as is, never tuned away.

negativeControls.rule: each control is run like the real comparison; it must FAIL, i.e. give fewer than pass.sunSitesWithin5 Sun sites within 5 points. A control that passes means the comparison cannot tell right from wrong.

controls.what: skyline mirrored east-west: mask[i] -> mask[(720 - i) % 720]
